title: Reserved pool headroom - 1:1 prep (scratchpad)
content:
Context / goal:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Jordan (capacity lead) + quick follow-ups for next weekly sync. Focus: reserved pool headroom, short-term reservations, and autoscaling guardrails.

High-level thesis (one-liner):
- Keep hosted latency SLAs by maintaining 10-15% reserved headroom on production GPU pools while using burst autoscale for short spikes to avoid overcommit spend.

Quick numbers snapshot (last 30 days):
- Committed GPUs (prod-dedicated): 160 x A100-40GB equivalent
- Avg utilization (4-week rolling): ~62%
- 95th percentile concurrent GPU demand (peak weekdays): 210 GPUs
- Current buffer = committed - p95_peak = 160 - 210 = -50 (i.e., 50 GPU shortfall during peaks)
- Spike profile: median spike duration ~22 minutes, 95th percentile spike ~2.1 hours
- Cost: spot/burst instance effective cost ~ $1.45 / GPU-hour; reserved committed amortized cost ~ $0.95 / GPU-hour

Simple forecast assumptions (for discussion):
- Traffic growth: 12% MoM (observed product triggers and new customer onboardings)
- If growth holds, p95 demand in 8 weeks -> ~ 210 * 1.12^2 ~= 263 GPUs
- Option A (conservative): ramp reservations to 220 GPUs over next 6 weeks (+60 GPUs) and rely on burst for remaining peaks
- Option B (cost-forward): keep reservations at 160, increase burst capacity and tighten autoscale latency SLOs to ensure cold-start < 30s; risk = cost volatility + potential transient throttles

Operational constraints / notes:
- Procurement lead time for dedicated reservations: ~3-4 weeks for contract + provisioning
- Dedicated SLA requires 99.9% availability for reserved pool; autoscale nodes are best-effort and do not count for reserved SLA
- Caching and batching improvements expected to reduce token-level cost by ~7% if we deploy prefix-KV tuning in next sprint

Autoscale policy ideas (draft):
- Base policy: maintain at least 10% headroom over 7-day rolling p75 demand (helps absorb small fluctuations)
- Spike policy: allow burst up to +50% of committed when cluster average latency < target and we have <60% spot utilization
- Cooldown: prefer scale-down cooldown = 8 minutes to avoid oscillation; if we see repeated oscillation, turn on 15m cooldown for that pool
- Pre-warm option: for predictable large night jobs, schedule pre-warm instances at T-20m for large batch runs

Questions to ask Jordan in 1:1:
- Do we want a short-term reservation increase request this quarter (yes/no), or do we prefer to rely on burst for next 8 weeks?
- If we increase reservations, what is the max procurement budget we can commit this quarter? Rough cap we discussed earlier: $75k/month additional commit? Need confirmation.
- Any signals from sales/CS about upcoming large customer onboardings that would materially change the forecast? (Priya / CS input?)
- Tolerance for transient throttles during peak (if we avoid reservations): what product teams can accept brief degraded throughput?

Follow-ups / action items (owner, due):
- [ ] Build a 12-week simple Monte Carlo spike simulation using past 90d minute-level concurrency to estimate tail risk (owner: Avery) due 2026-03-17
- [ ] Draft procurement request for +40 GPUs (A100 equiv) + cost / ROI blurb (owner: Jordan) due 2026-03-20
- [ ] Ask CS (Priya) for confirmed onboarding dates for top 5 customers flagged as high risk (owner: Priya) due 2026-03-12 (update: chasing via Slack)
- [ ] Add an alert that warns when p95 projected demand > committed GPUs for >3 consecutive days (owner: SRE -> create alert JIRA: JIRA-ENG-3012) due 2026-03-24
- [ ] Quick experiment: enable prefix-KV tuning on serving-runtime for one busy model to measure latency/cost delta (owner: infra/research -> link PR after spike test) due 2026-03-31

Notes / friction points to surface in meeting:
- Partial reservations (e.g., ability to reserve in 8-GPU increments) would help match demand granularity; procurement currently only supports 16/32 increments.
- Contract negotiation: want shorter flex window (90 days) on new commit so we can adjust if growth stalls. Finance likely pushes back; need arguments.
- Need clearer visibility for feature flags that cause short spikes (we still see 2-3 unknown spike sources each week). Tracking issue: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/issues/118

Rough cost math (back-of-envelope):
- If we add +60 GPUs reserved: incremental monthly hours = 60 * 24 * 30 = 43,200 GPU-hours/month. At $0.95/hr -> ~$41k/month. If reserved reduces burst spend by 60% we save ~$17k/month -> net add ~$24k/month. Need to confirm exact pricing tiers.

Meeting agenda (5-7m items, keep short):
- 0:00-0:03: Recap current headroom shortfall and p95 numbers
- 0:03-0:10: Present two options (ramp reservations vs rely on burst) + cost/risks
- 0:10-0:15: Decide on short-term procurement ask or runway to delay
- 0:15-0:18: Assign follow-ups and deadlines

Loose scratch calculations / what-if table (text):
- Table cols: committed | p95 demand | buffer | action
- Row1 (now): 160 | 210 | -50 | consider +40 reserve request
- Row2 (8w forecast): 160 | 263 | -103 | need >100 additional GPUs or heavy burst reliance
- Row3 (opt A): 220 | 263 | -43 | softer risk, maybe +40 commit instead of +100

Things to avoid saying bluntly in meeting (notes to self):
- Don’t promise immediate latency improvements from autoscale changes (we don’t have hard data yet)
- Avoid committing to procurement larger than we can fund for two quarters without a sales-commitment anchor

Slack snippets to send after meeting (copy/paste style):
- "Recap: agreed to draft +40 GPU procurement request; Avery to run Monte Carlo sim and Jordan to draft ask. Priya to confirm CS onboarding dates. SRE to add alert for p95 > committed for >3d. I'll post follow-up by EOD Friday."

Open data needs (where to source):
- Minute-level concurrency from observability (ask observability team for CSV export for last 90 days)
- Cost breakdown: billing team export for committed vs burst GPU spend last 90 days
- New customer onboarding timelines (CS roster)

Random thought-log (scratch):
- If we can shave 10% of token-level cost via KV tuning, that’s equivalent to ~16 reserved GPUs in cost-savings terms -> factor into 6-week decision.
- Could prototype a small reserved pool dedicated to high-QPS customers (isolated lane) to reduce tail interactions. Feels like a longer project (Q2).

End of scratchpad.
